title: Spray buffing with a rotary machine
audience: Trained cleaners who operate a rotary floor machine for spray buffing in any cleaning-group business.
learningOutcomes: Complete the electrical and pad pre-use checks for a spray buffer and record the results.
Select a pad by colour, using the manufacturer's guide and the task.
Use gloves, eye protection and ventilation when a spray buffing product is in use.
Connect and disconnect a spray buffer using the socket-switch sequence.
Stop, tag and report a faulty spray buffer.

instruction.heading: What spray buffing is, and what this version covers
instruction.body: Spray buffing combines a rotary machine, a pad and a light application of product to bring up the shine on a floor surface. It uses the same electrical equipment and chemical rules as floor buffing, and the source treats it as a separate procedure because of the product and the finish. This lesson covers the full procedure from the source: the equipment checks, pad selection, personal protection, ventilation, the connection sequence and the service sequence. Follow the steps in order, and check any product against its label and the manufacturer directions.

instruction.heading: Electrical and pad checks
instruction.body: Only trained employees use electrical equipment. Check the test label before use, and confirm that the plug, the flex and the casing are intact, with no bare wires or tape. Keep a register of machines. Select the pad by colour for the task, using the manufacturer's guide, because the darker the pad, the more abrasive it is. At the end of the task, repeat the safety checks, so that any damage caused during use is found.

instruction.heading: Products, protective equipment and ventilation
instruction.body: Wash and check all equipment before use, so that products are not mixed by accident. Wear gloves at all times when you use chemicals or handle pads and base plates. Wear goggles, because your hands and eyes can be exposed to product and dust. Open windows or doors where possible, so that people nearby are not breathing fumes. Keep customers away from the work area, and sign-post it.

instruction.heading: Connection sequence and service method
instruction.body: Before you plug the machine in, switch the socket off. When you unplug, switch the socket off before you remove the plug from the wall. The service sequence for spray buffing, including how product is applied, the order of passes, and any drying or rinsing step, is not yet written from the source. Until the sequence is approved, follow the written spray-buffing procedure your business supplies.

procedure: Complete the electrical pre-use check and the pad check, and record the test label date.
Select the pad by colour for the task, using the manufacturer's guide.
Wash and check all equipment, and confirm that no two products are being mixed.
Put on gloves and eye protection. Open ventilation where possible, and sign-post the area.
Confirm the socket is off, then plug the machine in.
Spray a small section close to the floor first, and buff its outer edges before working toward the centre of that section.
Wipe any overspray from the skirting boards with a clean, damp cloth as you go.
Start at the point furthest from the door, and work back toward the exit so that you do not walk over finished areas.
Keep the cable behind you at all times, so the pad cannot reach it. Never let the cable run over your shoulder.
Halfway through the task, switch the socket off and unplug the machine. Check the pad, and turn it to a clean face if it is dirty. Then switch the socket off, plug the machine back in, and continue.
Never leave the machine running unattended.
When the task is finished, sweep or mop up the debris that has come out from under the skirting boards.
Switch the socket off before unplugging. Repeat the safety checks on the machine and cable.
Store the machine upright with the pad off, clean and dry. Record any defect or fault.

workedExamples.situation: A spray buffer's pad is clean, but the flex shows a scuff near the plug.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. A damaged flex is a fault. Switch the socket off, unplug the machine, tag it faulty and report it. Do not tape the flex and carry on.

workedExamples.situation: Two products are on the trolley, and you are not sure which one the job requires.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not mix them, and do not guess. Read the labels and the SDS for both, confirm the approved product with the supervisor, and use only the product confirmed for the surface.

equipmentAndPpe: Gloves for chemicals, pads and base plates.
Spray buffer with a current test label.
Colour-coded pads and the manufacturer's colour guide.

commonErrors.error: Mixing products to suit the job.
commonErrors.prevention: Use one approved product, at its label dilution.
Use the colour guide and the job specification.

commonErrors.error: Working without eye protection because the spray seems light.
commonErrors.prevention: Goggles on whenever a product is in use.

commonErrors.error: Skipping a step in the service sequence, such as switching off before moving the cable.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the business's written spray-buffing procedure until the service sequence is approved.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Electrical equipment is tested and tagged as set out in “Safe use and care of electrical machines”.
Chemical use follows “Chemical competency: reading labels and safety data sheets”. The product's SDS governs its application rate, contact and personal protection.
Overspray and fumes: keep customers and property away from the work area and ventilate.
Wet floors remain a slip hazard until they are dry. Keep the warning signs up until the floor is confirmed dry.

qualityStandard: Pre-use electrical and pad checks completed and recorded.
Pad selected by colour for the task and checked before use.
Protective equipment worn, the area sign-posted, and customers kept back.
Socket-off connection and disconnection followed without prompting.
Service sequence followed in order as written in the procedure, with the cable kept behind the operator.
documentationEvidence: Pre-use check record for the machine and pad.
Pad change record, with the reason for the change.
summary: Check the test label, plug, flex and casing before the spray buffer is used.
Choose the pad by colour from the manufacturer's guide.
Gloves, goggles and ventilation whenever a product is in use.
Socket off before plugging in and before unplugging.

knowledgeChecks.question: Before you start a spray buffer, which check comes first?
options: That it switches on and the pad spins and the pad is the right colour
Its test label, and the condition of the plug, flex and casing
That the cable is long enough to reach the far corner

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does pad colour matter?
options: Pads of one colour are used across every floor type, so no choice is needed
Darker pads are more abrasive, so the choice must suit the task and the manufacturer's guide
It only shows which brand made the pad and it has no real effect on the floor finish

knowledgeChecks.question: The flex has a scuff near the plug. What should you do?
options: Tape the scuff and continue, because it is only cosmetic
Continue on a lower speed until the job is finished
Tag the machine as faulty, unplug it and report it
